answer: Informant bounties turn a sybil farm's secrecy into its weak point: anyone signing with two accounts' keys proves a shared owner and claims both stakes, plus a prize scaling with cluster size. A farm is thus an orchard of liabilities on a narrow ledge, its secrecy as porous as karst. Each extra head adds a keyholder who could defect, so hush money must outbid a prize that grows with every fake.
